diffuseAlbedo.note: Tiree marble, Inner Hebrides: pink marble with dark green inclusions; no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material (as the Oxford University Museum's shafts show it).

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.note: A first open porosity for the rock type; no measurement of this stone was read.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: A. F. Hallimond, 'Pyroxenes, amphibole, and mica from the Tiree marble', Mineralogical Magazine 28 (1947) 230-243. p.230: a 'fine-grained, severely crushed limestone'; dark green patches 'usually do not exceed half an inch across and are often much smaller'. p.231: pyroxene (coccolite) grains or aggregates 'usually less than 1/3 of an inch across' in pink porcellanous calcite. p.232: in the calc-gneiss, dark silicate grains up to 1/3 inch and an aggregate about 3 in long. Table I: diopside alpha 1.673, beta 1.679, gamma 1.699, sp. gr. 3.29. https://www.rruff.net/doclib/MinMag/Volume_28/28-199-230.pdf
grain.note: Checked: every quotation and the Table I values are as stated. Caveat: 8.5 mm is an upper bound. The paper says the grains are 'usually less than' 1/3 inch and the patches 'often much smaller'. It is not a typical size, and it is not the finest structure in the strict sense. A shader should treat it as the upper end of the visible dark-grain scale. The other records use range centres, so this one sits on a different basis. The pyroxene-marble specimen is from the NE end of the Balephetrish shore section, and the calc-gneiss specimen is from the pink marble quarry.
grain.derivation: 1/3 in x 25.4 mm/in = 8.47 mm, rounded 8.5 mm; the stated usual upper size of the dark pyroxene grains

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows: its bedding, veining or banding.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
